blockingFinding.headline: TaskView's Slack integration fires on TASK LIFECYCLE EVENTS, not on workflow states. It cannot be scoped to Blocked / Review / Verification / Done.
blockingFinding.fullCatalogue: 30 events in 5 categories: TASKS (7: created, assigned, status changed, completed, edited, added to sprint, deleted); SPRINTS (8); MEMBERS (3); TIME TRACKING (5); RECURRING RULES (7).
blockingFinding.noStateEvents: There is NO per-status toggle anywhere in the catalogue - no Blocked, no Review, no Verification, no Done. The nearest primitives are 'Task status changed', which fires on EVERY transition including Backlog, Ready, In Progress and Cancelled, and 'Task completed', which tracks the complete flag.
blockingFinding.consequence: The Phase 7 instruction to enable 'exactly these four workflow states' is not satisfiable in this product. Any four-state restriction must happen downstream (a Slack-side workflow/filter) or be accepted as broader-than-spec.

currentEventState.assessment: Three of the five enabled events are outside anything the owner asked for: Task created, Task assigned and Task deleted. Left as found - not changed.

options: A. Closest faithful subset: enable ONLY 'Task status changed' + 'Task completed' and turn off created/assigned/deleted. Covers every transition into Blocked, Review and Verification plus Done, but also fires on Backlog, Ready, In Progress and Cancelled. Broader than spec, no state-level filtering possible in TaskView.
B. Keep as-is (5 events) and accept the extra created/assigned/deleted noise.
C. Apply option A in TaskView and add a Slack-side workflow filter to drop transitions other than the four states, achieving the spec's intent outside TaskView.
D. Record on AF-S1403 that its acceptance criteria are not literally achievable and have the owner restate them in event terms.

githubIntegrationRepoint.verdict: BLOCKED - no safe supported operation exists. No mutation was attempted.
evidence: The integrations router exposes only: GET /module/integrations, POST (create via OAuth), DELETE, PATCH /toggle, PATCH /select-repo, POST /sync, GET /repos, OAuth init/callback and the provider webhooks. There is no move/rebind/change-project operation.

Project binding is fixed at OAuth time: getOAuthUrl(provider, projectId, userId) signs projectId into the OAuth state JWT and handleOAuthCallback reads it back. Rebinding therefore requires a brand-new OAuth authorisation, which needs the owner's own GitHub credentials.

selectRepo() calls syncIssues() and registerWebhook() immediately on repo selection (log line: 'repo selected, starting sync and webhook registration'). syncIssues imports repository issues as TaskView tasks, which would create roughly 59 duplicate tickets on goal 3 and break the 103-ticket invariant.
toggle() also calls syncIssues() whenever it is switched ON, so re-enabling is equally unsafe on a goal-3-bound integration.
registerWebhook() creates a NEW webhook on the GitHub repository, a GitHub-side settings mutation.
